cards.text: Ezekiel the prophet is among the exiles at Tel-abib by the River Kebar, where he's sat with them for seven days, overwhelmed (Ezekiel 3:15). At the end of those seven days the word of the LORD comes, and God gives him a job: "Son of man, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel." A watchman stands on the wall and shouts when trouble's coming, so congratulations, friend. Ezekiel just became the neighborhood's human smoke alarm.

cards.question: Ezekiel is now Israel's watchman. Whenever he hears a word from God's mouth, what is he supposed to give the people?

cards.text: Then God walks him through it, case by case. Case one: God says to a wicked man, "You will surely die," but Ezekiel never warns him.

cards.question: In case one, God tells a wicked man he will surely die. True or false: if Ezekiel stays quiet, that wicked man gets a pass because nobody warned him.
When the unwarned wicked man dies in his iniquity, God will hold ___ responsible for his blood.

cards.text: Case two. Ezekiel DOES warn the wicked man, and the man still won't turn from his wicked way, so he dies in his iniquity. That's the GPS yelling "TURN, TURN, TURN" and the driver just cruising straight into the lake.

cards.question: In case two, Ezekiel warned the wicked man, but the man wouldn't turn. Where does that leave Ezekiel?

cards.text: Case three flips it: a righteous man turns from his righteousness and commits iniquity, and God puts a stumbling block before him. Nobody warns him, he dies in his sin, and that line again: God holds Ezekiel responsible for his blood.

cards.question: True or false: the righteous man who turned to sin and was never warned still gets credit for the righteous acts he did before.

cards.text: Case four. Ezekiel warns a righteous man not to sin, and the man doesn't sin, and FINALLY I can stop wincing through my mustache.

cards.question: In case four, Ezekiel warned a righteous man not to sin, and he didn't. Why does that man live?

answers.text: Because of his past righteous acts

cards.text: There, the hand of the LORD is upon Ezekiel again, and God says, "Get up, go out to the plain, and there I will speak with you." A private meeting. When somebody tells me "we need to talk," I start sweating flour.

cards.question: Out on the plain, Ezekiel sees the ___ of the LORD, like what he saw by the River Kebar.
True or false: with the glory of the LORD right there on the plain, Ezekiel falls facedown.

cards.text: Then the Spirit enters him and sets him on his feet, word for word how it went back in Ezekiel 2:2. Facedown, back up, facedown, back up. This prophet is getting his steps in.

cards.question: Back on his feet, Israel's new watchman gets his next order from God. Where does God send him?

answers.text: Into his house to shut himself in
Up onto the city wall to watch

cards.text: Then God tells him, "And you, son of man, they will tie with ropes, and you will be bound so that you cannot go out among the people." A watchman stuck in the house, and friend, I did years in a junk drawer and nobody even bothered with ropes.

cards.question: God says He'll make Ezekiel's tongue stick to the roof of his mouth. What will that keep Ezekiel from doing?

cards.text: So God's got His finger on the mute button. When He speaks with Ezekiel, He'll open his mouth, and Ezekiel is to tell them, "This is what the Lord GOD says."

cards.question: True or false: God expects every single person in Israel to listen when Ezekiel speaks His words.
